newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends weaker as traders take profits.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends weaker as traders take profits.

text.p: London cocoa futures resumed their softer tone on Wednesday as trade houses and origins cashed in on the steep gains recorded on Tuesday.

The benchmark March contract met resistance early on as initial efforts to extend the rally faltered at 950 stg -- a one-month high -- disappointing players who went long hoping for a break on the upside, traders said.
Tuesday's rally which carried March above the technical barrier of 943 stg mainly involved short-covering and traders said fundamentals were not ripe yet to pull the market out of current range.
At the close, March cocoa stood 11 stg lower at 933 stg a tonne, the lowest for the day. Other contracts lost up to nine stg. Turnover totalled 6,807 lots including switches and AAs.
"It's mainly trade profit taking. Currency hasn't been an assist today," said one trader.
But in New York, sterling's retracement against the dollar was cited as the primary reason for speculative sales.
Sterling was off its session highs on Wednesday trading at $1.6385 in late dealings, but still above levels seen on Tuesday.
Cargill was said to be a good seller on Wednesday while Credie Lyonnais Rouse was buying.
Technically, March may find 955 stg a tough resistance on the upside.
Elsewhere, physical news was thin with demand expected to remain muted until early January unless prices fall dramatically, traders said.
